display.purpose: The wordmark and the 404 headline. Once per page at most; tracking is tight enough that letters nearly touch.

headline.purpose: Section titles, always paired with a mono index label above.

title.purpose: Card, project and journey-stage titles. Regular weight — size carries hierarchy.

lede.purpose: The single oversized paragraph opening About and anchoring Contact. Set in Paper White, not Muted Steel.

body.purpose: All reading text, in Muted Steel, capped near 65ch.

label.purpose: Mono, uppercase, wide-tracked. Section indices, metadata keys, status values, captions.

motion.name: ease-signature
motion.purpose: The system's only easing curve. Fast out, long settle — used for every reveal, tab change and card entrance.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: Card and control state changes: border, background, lift.

motion.name: duration-art
motion.purpose: Artwork scale inside a hovered card. Deliberately slower than its frame so the lift reads as depth.

motion.name: duration-reveal
motion.purpose: Scroll-triggered section reveals, 18px rise, fired once at -80px margin.

motion.name: duration-card-in
motion.purpose: Project-card entrance on filter change, staggered 45ms and capped at 320ms.

narrative.overview:
A dark room after hours with the work laid out on the table and one lamp over it. The surface you are looking at is a desk, not a dashboard: it has grain, it has a faint ruled grid, and it is mostly empty. Instruments are present — monospaced readouts, status rows, a terminal in the corner — but they sit at the edges of the room. The craft is what the light falls on.

Everything saturated in this system is a light source. Filament Violet is the lamp; Cold Cathode is the screen. Nothing else in the palette emits — the greys are all absorbed light, ranging from near-black desk to bright paper-white text. This is why accent use is so restrained: adding a third glowing colour would turn a studio into an arcade.

Density is deliberately uneven. Sections breathe at 6–8rem of vertical rest, then concentrate into tight 12-column arrangements where the content earns it. No section repeats the previous section's structure: a vertical tab rail follows an editorial two-column, which follows a dense bento grid. The consistency lives in the surface treatment, type scale and accent discipline — never in the layout.
keyCharacteristics: One texture across the entire site: a 72px ruled grid and film grain, both under 5% opacity
Zero shadows; depth is tonal layering plus hairline borders
Two accents only, both behaving as physical light
Editorial sans for everything a person reads; mono strictly for machine-adjacent text
Every composition legible with motion disabled

rules.name: The Two Lamps Rule
rules.body: Only two things in this system emit light: Filament Violet and Cold Cathode. Combined, they cover under 10% of any viewport. A third saturated hue is a system violation, not a design decision.

rules.name: The Absorbed Grey Rule
rules.body: Every non-accent colour is a step on one neutral ramp from #08080a to #e9e9ee. No coloured greys, no tinted surfaces, no separate border colour per component. Two hairline weights carry every division on the site.

rules.name: The Warm White Rule
rules.body: Text is #e9e9ee, never #ffffff. Pure white is reserved for the single case of text on a filled violet button, where it is compensating for saturation.

rules.name: The Machine Voice Rule
rules.body: Monospace is only for things a machine would say: labels, indices, status values, metadata, counts, terminal output, file paths, and placeholder markers. The moment text is a person talking, it is Inter.

rules.name: The Tighter As Bigger Rule
rules.body: Letter-spacing tightens monotonically with size: -0.055em at display, -0.03em at headline, -0.02em at title, normal at body, and +0.16em at label. A large heading at default tracking is the single most reliable tell of an undesigned page.

rules.name: The Index Rule
rules.body: Every section headline is preceded by a mono index label (01 — About). It is the site's spine: it tells the visitor where they are in a long scroll without a progress UI.

rules.name: The Shared Gutter Rule
rules.body: Every section, in every composition, aligns to the same shell. A section that breaks the gutter to go full-bleed must still align its inner content to it.

rules.name: The Empty Column Rule
rules.body: When a layout needs a sidebar, skip a column between it and the body rather than closing the gap. The empty column is load-bearing.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Depth comes from tone, edge and blur. If an element seems to need a shadow, it needs a tonal step or a stronger hairline instead.

rules.name: The Translucent Panel Rule
rules.body: Panels sit at 40–60% opacity over the textured ground so the grid stays continuous beneath them. A fully opaque panel breaks the illusion that the whole page is one surface.

rules.name: The Nested Step Rule
rules.body: A child container is always one radius step tighter than its parent (xl outside, lg inside). Matching radii across a nesting boundary flattens the hierarchy.

rules.name: The Pill Means Action Rule
rules.body: Fully-rounded means interactive or stateful. Nothing static is a pill, and nothing clickable is a rectangle.

dos: Do align every section to the shared shell (84rem, gutters 1.25rem / 2rem / 3rem), whatever its internal composition.
Do precede every section headline with a mono index label (04 — Cybersecurity).
Do tighten letter-spacing as type scales up, to -0.055em at display size.
Do build depth from tonal steps, hairlines and backdrop blur.
Do keep panels translucent (40–60%) so the grid texture stays continuous under them.
Do give each project card an explicit shape so the grid never reads as a uniform matrix.
Do move contained artwork slower than its frame on hover (700ms art, 300ms card).
Do label every placeholder in the UI where a visitor can see it.
Do gate every animation on prefers-reduced-motion and verify the composition still holds with motion off.
donts: Don't add a box-shadow. This system has none, anywhere.
Don't introduce a third saturated colour, or push violet and ice past ~10% of a viewport combined.
Don't use pure #ffffff for text except on a filled violet button.
Don't set body copy, headlines or prose in JetBrains Mono. Mono is the machine's voice only.
Don't put more than one primary (Paper White filled) button in a viewport.
Don't express skill or progress as a percentage, bar or ring.
Don't show a success state for anything that was not actually delivered.
Don't repeat a previous section's structure; the consistency is in the surface, not the layout.
Don't render a bare grey box where an image is missing — draw generated art at the correct aspect ratio instead.
